# dsh-team-progress

A DeepSeek Harness GUI plugin showing four views of a running agent team, counted from
durable state

: who is on what, which defects are tracked, how far the goal has moved,
and what needs a human now.

A source it cannot read renders `unavailable` with the
reason instead of a `0`.

The host half (`lib/index.js`) registers one loopback JSON route
`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` on th

e `webServer` service; the client half
(`lib/client.js`) registers the panel with the slot service a

nd re-reads that route
every 5 seconds while the panel is open.

## What it adds

- **MEMBERS** — one row per member: live status, the shared task it claims, that
task's status. A me

mber holding nothing renders `no claimed task`.
- **DEFECTS** — counts by status across the configur

ed defect logs, plus the rows
still open. Recognised: `open` / `in flight` / `fixed` / `closed as su

begun against the cap, the phase, and `armed` / `disarmed`.
- **STALLED / BLOCKED** — the action lis

t, rendered first because a stall is the only
state that asks for a decision.
- **One RPC route** —

`POST /api/team-progress/rpc`, methods `state` and `act`.
- **One optional action surface** — comple

te / reopen / claim / release / reassign, wake,
interrupt, spawn, auto-assign, broadcast, member cap

, all through the same domain
methods the model's own tools call. Off by default; see Security.
## Requirements

The read path was traced against **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-24), and the
plugin was la

st exercised end to end on **0.2.1-rc.5** (2026-11-03): a
`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` with `{"meth

od":"state"}` answered `200` with a live
payload. No minimum version is declared.

- The client half is declared for the `web` platform (`dsh.client.platform`). It is
browser-plane co

de, so importing `dsh-team-progress/client` in Node fails with
`window is not defined` — that is the

plane, not a defect.
- Only `webServer` is a hard injection. `agents`, `agentTeams`, `sessionProjec

tions`,
`goals`, `sessionQuery` and `uiWorkspace` are resolved lazily, so a profile with one
of thos
e bundles disabled still loads the panel and reports the source.

`dsh.bundle.patch`

(`./cordis.patch.yml`) and the client bundle (`./lib/client.js`,
platform `web`).

**1. Clone, then make the package resolvable to the profile.** A profile resolves

om its own `package.json`, so add the checkout as a `link:`

## Security: the action surface

`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` is registered **directly on the web server, outside the
app's own auth

middleware.** With `allowMutations: true`, any local process — any
script, any tool, any agent on t

he machine — can drive the team board through this
route: complete, reopen, claim or reassign a shar

ed task, wake an inactive member,
interrupt a running agent, spawn a teammate, broadcast to the whol

, wake an inactive member,
interrupt a running agent, spawn a teammate, broadcast to the whole team.

- The shipped default is **off** (`allowMutations: false`).
- With it off, `act` answers **`403 TEAM

_PROGRESS_ACTIONS_DISABLED`** and reaches no
domain method. The read views, the counts and the read

path keep working unchanged.
- Turn it on deliberately, on a single-user machine, and treat the rout

e as a local
control socket rather than an authenticated API.
- `actionPolicy: 'read-write'` narrows

it further without turning it off: `spawn` and
`member-limit` answer **`403 TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTION_WI

THHELD`** while every board action
keeps working. Those two are the ones that outlive the click — on

e creates a live
agent with model budget attached, the other rewrites a config file on disk.
Withhol

ding is opt-in, so the value an existing profile already means (`'all'`) stays
the default rather th
an being re-interpreted under it.

Paths in `defectLogs` come from config only, never from the request, so the route
cannot be turned i
nto an arbitrary-file reader. The body is capped at 64 KiB.
